headline.text: Across overlapping treatment categories and procedure records, Länsi-Uusimaa lags national values in its crude life-prolonging treatment share and crude recorded MDT meeting share, though MDT figures measure recording practice.

details.text: In overlapping treatment categories, the county's crude life-prolonging treatment share is 25.2% (95% CI 22.7–27.9; n=267/1058) alongside the national 30.4% (4522/14873), and the 95% confidence interval excludes the national value.

Across overlapping treatment categories where a patient can have several treatments, Länsi-Uusimaa's crude curative share is 31.9% (95% CI 29.1–34.7; n=337/1058), with the 95% confidence interval excluding and exceeding the national 27.0% (4009/14873), while its crude symptomatic share is 40.1% (95% CI 37.2–43.1; n=424/1058), with the 95% confidence interval including the national 39.5% (5871/14873).

The crude share of patients with a recorded MDT meeting is 0.2% (95% CI 0.1–0.7; n=2/1058), whose 95% confidence interval excludes the national 6.0% (893/14873), but MDT records measure recording practice, not care, because specialist procedures enter HILMO only from direct patient contacts.

headline.text: Public county data omit wait times, referrals and primary care visits, and crude treatment shares cannot be stage-adjusted because stage is missing for about 48% of patients.

details.text: County shares are crude and have separate limitations: they are not age-adjusted (digitised age-adjusted figures from Kuva 16, at ±0.5 percentage points precision, exist for curative treatment only, by sex, with national lines at 26.7% for men and 26.9% for women), and separately they cannot be stage-adjusted because stage at diagnosis is missing for about 48% of patients.

The crude share with no treatment record within 12 months is 28.5% (95% CI 25.9–31.3; n=302/1058), with its 95% confidence interval including the national 27.5% (4089/14873); this mixes untreated patients and treatment that was not recorded, while a journal article finding about 90% HILMO and Cancer Registry concordance applies to diagnoses only.

Public report data do not measure symptoms, referrals or treatment start dates by county, primary care visits are not included in the report's data, occupational health is not mentioned at all, and imaging appears only indirectly because about 20% of patients are diagnosed on clinical examination alone, such as imaging.

In preliminary, unpublished national averages (not county-specific), lung cancer takes 155 days from symptoms to treatment in Finland compared with 107 days in Sweden and 67 days in Denmark, with 56 days of patient delay, 41 days in primary care and 58 days in specialist care.

headline.text: The team recommends publishing stage, drug and MDT coding coverage, tracking THL Ohjaus 21/2016 access times with handover alerts, and adopting a referral template with a diagnostic contact person.

details.text: Given Länsi-Uusimaa's crude recorded MDT share of 0.2% (95% CI 0.1–0.7; n=2/1058) versus 6.0% (893/14873) nationally, its crude life-prolonging share of 25.2% (95% CI 22.7–27.9; n=267/1058) versus 30.4% (4522/14873) across overlapping treatment categories, and missing stage for about 48% of patients, the team recommends publishing per-county stage, drug treatment and MDT recording coverage as data-quality signals.

Because the Health Care Act sets no legal maximum time for a cancer suspicion and uniform diagnostic timetables are lacking, the team recommends reporting access times using THL Ohjaus 21/2016 definitions for 16 cancers and flagging stalled handovers, while the Filha programme's diagnostics recommendation with recommended time limits is to be carried out before the 2030 mid-term evaluation.

Backed by mentor insight that a weak referral gets a lower urgency rating and by KYS's regional pathway document, the team recommends adopting a KYS-style referral template and referring persistent unexplained symptoms for a pulmonologist assessment after a normal X-ray, while under measure 2.5.2 the STM roadmap plans standardised referral criteria and symptom-based models by 2026–2028.

Because no reviewed regional pathway document names a diagnostic-phase contact person, the team recommends naming a contact person from referral to diagnosis, while under measure 1.2.3 the STM roadmap plans guidance on a named care-coordinator model by 2026–2028 that counties adopt by 2029–2031 without specifying the care phase.

rec:1.claim_text: Team recommendation 1: Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts. Each wellbeing services county reports lung cancer access times (referral → first specialist visit → diagnosis → treatment start) using the definitions in THL's Hoitoonpääsyn seuranta syövän hoidossa (Ohjaus 21/2016). Until national target times exist, flag stalled handovers.
rec:1.location: §1. Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts

rec:2.claim_text: Team recommendation 2: A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact. Adopt a standard referral content list and template, modelled on KYS. • Add a rule for primary care: if symptoms persist after a normal X-ray, refer for a pulmonologist assessment. • Name a contact person for the diagnostic phase, from referral to diagnosis.
rec:2.location: §2. A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact

rec:3.claim_text: Team recommendation 3: Report recording completeness per county: stage, drug treatment, MDT coding. Publish, per county, how completely stage, drug treatment and MDT meetings are recorded. Read county ‘gaps’ in these fields as data-quality signals first.
